```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
library(sf)
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
```

```{r}
GenderData <- read_csv(
  here("05w4_hw", "HDR25_Composite_indices_complete_time_series.csv")
)

head(names(GenderData), 20)
```
```{r}
GenderData %>%
  dplyr::select(iso3, country, gii_2010, gii_2019) %>%
  head()
```
```{r}
WorldMap <- st_read(
  here("05w4_hw", "world_countries.geojson")
)

names(WorldMap)
```
```{r}
WorldMap %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::select(COUNTRY, ISO) %>%
  head()
```
```{r}
library(countrycode)

WorldMap <- WorldMap %>%
  mutate(
    iso3 = countrycode(ISO, "iso2c", "iso3c")
  )

WorldMap %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::select(COUNTRY, ISO, iso3) %>%
  head()
```
```{r}
GenderChange <- GenderData %>%
  dplyr::select(iso3, country, gii_2010, gii_2019) %>%
  mutate(gii_change = gii_2019 - gii_2010)

WorldGender <- WorldMap %>%
  left_join(GenderChange, by = "iso3")

WorldGender %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::select(COUNTRY, gii_2010, gii_2019, gii_change) %>%
  head()
```
```{r}
nrow(WorldGender)

GenderChange %>%
  filter(!is.na(gii_2010), !is.na(gii_2019)) %>%
  anti_join(st_drop_geometry(WorldMap), by = "iso3") %>%
  dplyr::select(iso3, country)
```
```{r}
nrow(WorldGender)

GenderChange %>%
  filter(
    nchar(iso3) == 3,
    !is.na(gii_2010),
    !is.na(gii_2019)
  ) %>%
  anti_join(st_drop_geometry(WorldMap), by = "iso3") %>%
  dplyr::select(iso3, country)
```
```{r}
WorldGender %>%
  dplyr::select(COUNTRY, iso3, gii_2010, gii_2019, gii_change) %>%
  st_write(
    here("05w4_hw", "gender_inequality_change.geojson"),
    delete_dsn = TRUE
  )
```
```{r}
SavedMap <- st_read(
  here("05w4_hw", "gender_inequality_change.geojson")
)

nrow(SavedMap)
names(SavedMap)
```

Data and method

Gender Inequality Index (GII) data for 2010 and 2019 were obtained from the UNDP HDR25 composite indices time-series dataset. World boundaries were obtained from Esri's World Countries Generalized dataset. Country codes were converted from ISO two-letter to three-letter codes using the countrycode package before joining the datasets.

The new variable, gii_change, equals GII in 2019 minus GII in 2010. Negative values indicate lower gender inequality in 2019; positive values indicate higher inequality. Missing values were retained rather than replaced with zero.

The output retains all 251 boundary features. All countries with three-letter codes and non-missing GII values in both years matched a boundary feature.

Reproduction

Install sf, tidyverse, here, countrycode, and rmarkdown. Keep the supplied folder structure, open RStudio at the repository root, and Knit gender_inequality.Rmd. The analysis creates gender_inequality_change.geojson, containing the boundaries, country codes, GII values for both years, and their difference.
